verification_scope_reason: Actual local Windows restricted token permits workspace writes, denies outside writes, rejects model child breakaway, enforces a 64 MiB private memory cap, and kills restricted descendants when the host owner closes. Existing runner filesystem/private-temp/default-ACL/descendant and canonical process/control/budget consumers passed. Custom runner argv/failure contracts stay unchanged; invalid resource inputs are rejected.
adaptation: Explicit local sandbox confine_process(argv, policy, memory_bytes) extension. Only the native Windows provider opts into a breakaway-enabled trusted outer Job; its suspended restricted child leaves that Job and is assigned a separate non-breakaway memory/kill Job before resumption. Killing the trusted runner closes its child Job. Ordinary confine and other/custom providers retain their contracts. This avoids requiring nested Jobs on Windows 7; execution here used the current Windows host, not a Win7 guest or release qualification.
